source: BC Mathematics 6 content standard: combinations of transformations; original
prompt_latex: \text{Points P(2, 3), Q(4, 1) and R(2, 1) are reflected across the vertical line x = 5. Give the new points.}
prompt_plain: Points P(2, 3), Q(4, 1) and R(2, 1) are reflected across the vertical line x = 5. Give the new points.

prompt_parts.text: Points P(2, 3), Q(4, 1) and R(2, 1) are reflected across the vertical line x = 5. Give the new points.

worked_solution: A reflected point is the same distance from the line, on the other side, at the same height
P is 5 − 2 = 3 left of the line, so P′ is 3 right: x = 5 + 3 = 8
Q is 5 − 4 = 1 left of the line, so Q′ has x = 5 + 1 = 6
R is also 3 left, so R′ has x = 8. The y-values do not change

worked_solution: The x-values stay the same. Each y-value moves to the same distance on the other side of y = 4
D: 4 − 1 = 3 below the line, so 4 + 3 = 7, giving D′(1, 7)

source: BC Mathematics 6 content standard: combinations of transformations; original
prompt_latex: \text{Points A(6, 5), B(7, 4) and C(6, 2) are rotated 180° about the point (4, 4). Give the new points.}
prompt_plain: Points A(6, 5), B(7, 4) and C(6, 2) are rotated 180° about the point (4, 4). Give the new points.

prompt_parts.text: Points A(6, 5), B(7, 4) and C(6, 2) are rotated 180° about the point (4, 4). Give the new points.

worked_solution: A 180° turn about (4, 4) sends each point straight through (4, 4) to the other side, the same distance away
A is 2 right and 1 up from (4, 4), so A′ is 2 left and 1 down: (4 − 2, 4 − 1) = (2, 3)
B is 3 right and 0 up, so B′ is 3 left: (4 − 3, 4) = (1, 4)
C is 2 right and 2 down, so C′ is 2 left and 2 up: (4 − 2, 4 + 2) = (2, 6)

source: BC Mathematics 6 content standard: combinations of transformations; original
prompt_latex: \text{Points K(5, 4), L(5, 6) and M(6, 4) are rotated 90° clockwise about the point (4, 4). Give the new points.}
prompt_plain: Points K(5, 4), L(5, 6) and M(6, 4) are rotated 90° clockwise about the point (4, 4). Give the new points.

prompt_parts.text: Points K(5, 4), L(5, 6) and M(6, 4) are rotated 90° clockwise about the point (4, 4). Give the new points.

worked_solution: Measure each point from the centre (4, 4). A clockwise quarter turn sends 'right' to 'down' and 'up' to 'right'
K is 1 right of the centre, so K′ is 1 down: (4, 4 − 1) = (4, 3)
L is 1 right and 2 up, so L′ is 1 down and 2 right: (4 + 2, 4 − 1) = (6, 3)
M is 2 right, so M′ is 2 down: (4, 4 − 2) = (4, 2)

prompt_plain: A triangle has corners at (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 4). It is translated 2 right and 1 up, then reflected across the vertical line x = 6. Give the final corners.

prompt_parts.text: A triangle has corners at (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 4). It is translated 2 right and 1 up, then reflected across the vertical line x = 6. Give the final corners.

worked_solution: Translate: add 2 to x and 1 to y
Reflect across x = 6: each point goes the same distance to the other side of the line, at the same height
(3, 2) is 3 left of the line, so it goes 3 right to (9, 2). (5, 2) is 1 left, so it goes to (7, 2). (3, 5) is 3 left, so it goes to (9, 5)
